_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Executive Summary
Arbuckle LPG Rail Terminal,
Midstream Energy Partners (CA) Ltd.

The facility, currently owned and operated by Midstream Energy Partners (CA) Ltd. ("Midstream"). The site functions as a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal, where propane is delivered by railcar, stored in four pressurized tanks (total fill capacity of all four tanks: 306,000 gallons), and transferred to trucks for distribution. Facility operations are subject to the California Occupational Safety and Health Administration (Cal/OSHA) Process Safety Management (PSM) standard (Title 8 CCR §5189), and to the California Accidental Release Prevention Program (CalARP) under Title 19 CCR §2735. This is classified as a Federal Risk Management Program (RMP) and CalARP Program Level 3 process, due to the storage of propane  a regulated flammable substance  in quantities exceeding the 10,000-pound threshold, and the facilitys coverage under Cal/OSHA PSM regulations.

THE FACILITY AND THE REGULATED SUBSTANCE HANDLED
The Arbuckle LPG Rail Terminal receives LPG delivered by railcar and stores it in four pressurized LPG storage tanks, each with a maximum fill limit of 76,500 gallons. LPG is subsequently loaded onto trucks for distribution. To minimize emissions during loading and unloading operations, a vapor balance and recovery system is employed to reduce the release of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The facility operates continuously, 24 hours per day, serving propane distribution. 
The worst-case flammable scenario for the facility is based on the release of 76,500 gallons (314,415 pounds) of propane from a single storage tank. Propane, a regulated flammable substance under both the RMP and CalARP, is stored in quantities that classify the facility as a Program Level 3 process.
ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM
The accidental release prevention program is based on the requirements of Title 40 Code of Federal Regulation, Part 68 and Title 19 CCR §2735 and §2755. The program includ

es the following elements: Offsite Consequence Analysis, Employee Participation, Process Safety Information, Process hazard Analysis, Operating Procedures, Training, Contractor Evaluation, Contractors and Visitor Orientation, Pre-job Start-up Safety Review, Mechanical Integrity, Code of Safe Work Practices (Hot Work Permit, Confined Space Entry, and Control of Hazardous Energy), Management of Change, Incident Investigation, Emergency Planning and Response, and Compliance Audits. 
Midstream maintains an emergency response plan in compliance with local emergency response agencies. 
Midstream has a Hazardous Materials Business Plan on file with the Colusa County Environmental Health Services Department, which is the Certified Unified Program Agency for Colusa County.
Training includes employee responsibilities in the PSM and CalARP programs, emergency response, hot work permit procedures, code of safe work practices, and operating procedures.
The process maintains mitigation measures consisting of relief valves, check valves, manual shut off valves, automatic shutoffs, startup and operating procedures, grounding equipment, and containment area.

EXTERNAL EVENTS ANALYSIS
An earthquake is a possible external event at the facility. The facility has been designed and constructed in accordance with 2022 CBC with ASCE 7-16. Seismic loading was considered using seismic category D, risk category II, importance factor of 1.00. As part of an external events evaluation, the U.S. Geological Surveys Quaternary Fault and Fold Database indicates the site is near a Class B fault. Blass B faults show evidence of Quaternary deformation but may not extend deep enough to produce significant seismic events, or current data is insufficient for classification as a higher-risk fault.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICY
An accidental release prevention and emergency response policy have been established by Midstream management and implemented by the employees. In the

event of an accidental release, the facility operators are trained to shut off the source from a safe location or activate on of the emergency shutdown devices, contact 911, and secure the area. The 911 system is used to notify the Fire Department.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
Midstream maintains an emergency response plan in compliance with local emergency response agencies. The Arbuckle LPG Rail Terminal has a Hazardous Materials Business Plan on file with the Colusa County Environmental Health Services Department, the Certified Unified Program Agency for Colusa County. 

FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
This is a newly constructed facility and has not had any accidental releases as defined by Title 19 CCR §2735.4. 

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Planned changes to improve safety have been established based on process safety management audits and the process hazard analysis.

WORST CASE SCENARIO
A worst-case flammable release scenario was modeled for propane, a regulated flammable gas stored in a pressurized process at quantities above the 10,000-pound threshold. The scenario involved the catastrophic failure of a single storage tank containing 314,415 pounds of propane. Using the EPAs browser-based RMP*Comp tool, the 1 psi overpressure endpoint distance was calculated to be 0.5 miles. Based on population estimates from MARPLOT, this distance includes one housing unit and an estimated three residents, qualifying as offsite public receptors. Due to the presence of public receptors, the flammable nature of the substance, and the facility's coverage under Cal/OSHAs PSM standard, this process is classified as a Program Level 3 under both EPAs Risk Management Program and CalARP regulations.
ALTERNATE RELEASE SCENARIO
An alternative flammable release scenario was modeled for propane, based on a rupture or disconnection in a transfer hose during loading operations. The scenario involves the release of approximately 479 pounds of propane, which could lead to a vapor cloud

explosion (VCE). Using the EPA's ALOHA modeling software, the 1 psi overpressure endpoint distance was estimated at 0.04 miles. Based on population data from MARPLOT, this distance does not include any public receptors. This scenario represents a more realistic, though less severe, event compared to the worst-case scenario and helps inform emergency planning and mitigation strategies. 
MANAGEMENT COMMITMENT
Midstream has a commitment to employee and public safety. This commitment is demonstrated by maintaining the implementation of the process and safety requirements already in place. Furthermore, the resources invested in accident prevention, such as training personnel and considering safety in design during construction and installations, is an investment in good business practices. Midstream's policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable release. However, if a release does occur, trained personnel will respond to control and contain the release.
